title: The Harbour That Learned to Bend
instructions: 本材料为原创模拟教学材料，非官方雅思试题，也不代表任何官方分数。请先通读文章，理解海边社区如何为不确定性做规划。然后完成10道阅读题（单选、填空、判断正误/未提及）。语法部分先看中文讲解，再完成8道独立新句子的语法题。最后进行口语和写作迁移练习。所有答案和解释在末尾，请先自己做题。
passage:
In the small coastal town of Marrow Bay, life had always followed the tide. Fishermen left before dawn, cafés opened at nine, and the summer visitors arrived in July. But last year, a series of winter storms changed the conversation. The sea wall cracked in two places, and the council announced that repairs would cost more than the town could easily afford. At a packed public meeting in the old boathouse, the mayor, Elena Marsh, stood up and said something that surprised many people. 'We cannot predict the next storm,' she told the crowd. 'But we can decide how we will respond. If we wait for perfect information, we will wait forever.'

Her words started a long argument. Some residents wanted a taller sea wall immediately. Others argued that a wall would only push the problem along the coast. A retired teacher, Mr. Chen, suggested a different approach. 'If we plant more grass and trees along the dunes,' he said, 'the sand will hold better during high tides.' A young engineer named Priya agreed, but she added a condition. 'This will only work if we also improve the drainage system. Otherwise, water will simply collect behind the dunes.' The meeting ended without a decision, but it did produce a small planning group.

Over the next three months, the group met every Thursday in the library. They invited experts, read reports, and walked the shoreline with local volunteers. One idea that gained support was a 'living shoreline': a mix of rocks, sand, and native plants designed to absorb wave energy. It was cheaper than a concrete wall, and it could be adjusted as conditions changed. However, it required regular maintenance, and not everyone was convinced. 'If the council doesn't pay for the upkeep,' one shop owner warned, 'the whole thing will fall apart in five years.'

Elena Marsh proposed a compromise. The town would build a short section of living shoreline as a pilot project, and it would also raise the lowest part of the existing wall. 'This is not a final answer,' she said. 'It is a first step. If the pilot works, we can expand it. If it doesn't, we will have learned something useful.' The council approved a modest budget, and work began in early spring.

By August, the pilot section was complete. It was not beautiful, but it was functional. During a moderate storm in September, the new section held up well, while a small area of the old wall needed minor repairs. The town did not declare victory. Instead, the planning group published a short report with three recommendations: continue monitoring, set aside money each year for maintenance, and review the plan every two years. 'We are not trying to control the sea,' Elena wrote in the report's introduction. 'We are trying to live with it more intelligently.'

The story of Marrow Bay is not about a perfect solution. It is about a community that chose to act despite uncertainty. The residents did not agree on everything, and they still don't. But they created a process that allows them to change their minds as new evidence appears. In a world where the climate is shifting, that may be the most valuable skill of all.

grammar.title: 第一、第二条件句的常见用途；建议与可能性的表达
grammar.explanation: 英语条件句用来表达“如果……就……”。第一条件句（if + 一般现在时，主句用 will/can/may + 动词原形）表示真实、可能发生的未来情况，常用于提出建议、警告或承诺。例如：If we plant more trees, the sand will hold better. 第二条件句（if + 一般过去时，主句用 would/could/might + 动词原形）表示假设的、不太可能或想象的情况，常用于委婉建议或推测可能性。例如：If the council paid for upkeep, the project would last longer. 注意：条件从句中不用 will 或 would；建议可用 should, could, might, why don't we 等表达；可能性可用 may, might, could, probably 等。
grammar.example: If we plant more grass and trees along the dunes, the sand will hold better during high tides.

questions.prompt: If the town ______ more volunteers, the beach clean-up will finish faster.
questions.explanation: 第一条件句：if 从句用一般现在时 finds，主句用 will finish。
questions.evidence: 第一条件句结构：if + 一般现在时，主句 will + 动词原形。

questions.prompt: If I ______ you, I would join the planning group.
questions.explanation: 第二条件句表示假设，if I were you 是固定委婉建议表达。
questions.evidence: 第二条件句：if + 一般过去时（be 动词常用 were），主句 would + 动词原形。

questions.prompt: You ______ talk to the council about the drainage problem. It might help.
questions.evidence: 建议表达可用 should + 动词原形。

questions.prompt: If it rains tomorrow, the outdoor meeting ______ moved inside.
questions.explanation: 第一条件句表示真实可能的未来，主句用 will be。
questions.evidence: 第一条件句主句用 will + 动词原形。

questions.prompt: If we had more money, we ______ build a taller wall.
questions.explanation: 第二条件句表示假设情况，主句用 could + 动词原形表示可能性。
questions.evidence: 第二条件句主句可用 would/could/might + 动词原形。

questions.prompt: Why ______ we ask the experts for advice?
questions.explanation: Why don't we...? 是提出建议的常用句型。
questions.evidence: 建议表达可用 Why don't we + 动词原形？

questions.prompt: The project ______ succeed, but we need more information first.
questions.explanation: might 表示可能性，语气比 may 更不确定。

questions.prompt: If the pilot ______ well, we will expand it next year.
questions.explanation: 第一条件句：if 从句用一般现在时 works，主句用 will expand。
questions.evidence: 第一条件句：if + 一般现在时，主句 will + 动词原形。
